stations.challenge: Your friend wants to plan every day; you want to decide each morning. Agree on the first week.
followUpQuestions: What makes the first week of summer special?
Do you prefer making plans or being spontaneous?
Does a long break feel different from a short one?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: Is total freedom always as enjoyable as it sounds?
stations.stretch: Plan a weekly summer routine with time for rest, for friends and for one useful activity.
stations.subtitle: Two months, no timetable.
stations.title: The First Day of Freedom

stations.challenge: You have seven days and a small budget. Negotiate a holiday you would both enjoy.
followUpQuestions: What was your most memorable summer trip?
Is the destination or the company more important?
What could you discover in your own region?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: Is a trip abroad always better than a holiday at home?
stations.stretch: Plan a cheap adventure in your own region and explain why it could be better than a trip abroad.
stations.subtitle: Adventure does not need a passport.
stations.title: Travel or Stay at Home?

stations.challenge: One friend feels left out when the group plans a trip. What can the group do?
followUpQuestions: How do you keep in touch when friends travel?
Why can family holidays be both fun and difficult?
How much time alone do you need?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: How can you balance friends, family and time alone?
stations.stretch: Is spending a lot of time alone in summer good or bad? Give reasons for both sides.
stations.subtitle: Who gets your summer hours?
stations.title: Friends, Family and Me Time

stations.challenge: You can work for four weeks or volunteer for two weeks. Choose, explain and try to agree with your partner.
followUpQuestions: What could you learn from a part-time job?
Would you choose more money or more free time?
Should students be expected to earn their own spending money?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: Is earning money worth giving up your free time?
stations.stretch: Some students have to work in summer and others don’t need to. Is that fair? What could schools do?
stations.subtitle: Cash, skills or free time?
stations.title: Summer Jobs and Money

stations.challenge: Your group wants a weekend without screens, but one friend refuses. Agree on three simple rules.
followUpQuestions: Do your screen habits change during the holidays?
Can gaming with friends count as social time?
Would a phone-free day be difficult for you?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: Is a week without your phone a good idea or impossible?
stations.stretch: Suggest a fair rule for using phones on a family holiday.
stations.subtitle: A summer online – or offline?
stations.title: Screens, Gaming and Switching Off

stations.challenge: Your friend thinks everyone else is having a better holiday. Give practical advice.
followUpQuestions: When is boredom useful?
Why do people post their best moments online?
How can you enjoy a quiet day without feeling guilty?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: Can boredom actually be good for you?
stations.stretch: Explain why a quiet summer can be just as good as an exciting one.
stations.subtitle: Doing nothing can be something.
stations.title: Boredom, Rest and FOMO

stations.challenge: Tell a one-minute summer story with a surprising ending. Your partner asks two questions.
followUpQuestions: What made your last summer memorable?
Do unexpected events often become the best stories?
Would you rather take photos or just enjoy the moment?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: What makes an ordinary day unforgettable?
stations.stretch: Tell the same story again from the point of view of another person who was there.
stations.subtitle: The stories we bring back.
stations.title: Summer Memories and Surprises

stations.challenge: Suggest one change to the summer holidays at your school. Try to persuade your partner.
followUpQuestions: What do you find hardest about returning to school?
Can two months away help you learn better?
What would you change about your next summer?
languageSupport: How would you feel about that?
stations.mainQuestion: Are two months of summer holidays too long, too short or just right?
stations.stretch: What could students do in summer so that they don’t forget what they have learned? Suggest three ideas.
stations.subtitle: What stays after the holidays end?
stations.title: Back to School: Was It Worth It?

toolkit.example: On the one hand …, on the other …
What would you choose and why?

vocabulary.explanation: a short break away from home
work without pay to help others
a regular way of doing things
lose a chance to take part

warmUp.note: If you want: a short activity to start.
warmUp.prompt: Imagine you have two completely free months. Choose your top three priorities and compare them.

metadata.title: Summer Holidays: Two Months of Freedom

ui.lessonGoal: Express opinions, explain reasons and ask follow-up questions.
ui.levelTip: Choose about 5 stations. Give a reason for each answer and ask one follow-up question.

presentation.introduction: Two months without school. Adventure, rest, friends, money, boredom, memories. What makes summer holidays genuinely worth remembering?
presentation.privacyNotice: You can invent examples. No one has to share private family plans, finances, locations or personal experiences.
quickStart: Give a reason or an example.
Ask your partner a follow-up question.
Open the challenge if you need more to discuss.
presentation.strap: How will you spend your summer?
presentation.subtitle: A conversation, not a test
